headline: Learned models reconcile bulk, single-cell and multi-omic measurement layers
label: Deep Learning For Omics Analysis
summary: Deep learning methods are now benchmarked and applied across bulk, single-cell and multi-omic data to address platform and modality heterogeneity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reconciling heterogeneous measurement layers, whether bulk versus single-cell, platform versus platform, or across omic modalities, through learned representations rather than assuming comparability. TransPlatformer translates fold-change profiles from legacy microarrays to current platforms, and TwinPurify uses adjacent-normal profiles as background to purify bulk tumor transcriptomes. In single-cell settings, scMDCF harmonizes cross-modality representations, hierarchical cross-entropy improves out-of-distribution annotation, and DeltaNMF separates baseline from disease-specific gene programs. Several items emphasize interpretability and benchmarking, including scGeneLens for dissecting single-cell foundation models and a systematic assessment finding that a simple Random Forest matches more complex models for structural variant filtering. Other items, including MapPFN, ESFS, PIMO and LaCoGSEA, address adjacent problems without explicit cross-layer comparison. What is new is the breadth of learned approaches applied across these layers, with benchmarking against simpler baselines.
